c.tagline: West Bohemia's grand belle-époque spa town of thermal springs, colonnades and Becherovka

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered but agree a price for longer trips. Ride-hailing (Uber/Bolt) is limited outside Prague, so a phoned or ranked taxi is usually the reliable option in Karlovy Vary.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-wide emergency number and connects to English-speaking operators. Dial 155 for an ambulance and 158 for the police directly.

hood_landmark.Lázeňské centrum: Mill Colonnade Mlynska kolonada Karlovy Vary
hood_landmark.Tuhnice: Tuhnice Karlovy Vary Ohre river KV Arena

avoid.reason: Agree taxi fares or use apps to avoid overcharging, and skip poor-rate currency exchange booths along the spa colonnades.

hood_desc: The Lázeňské centrum (spa district) is the postcard heart of Karlovy Vary: belle-époque facades in pastel colors line the Teplá river, and grand colonnades shelter a dozen thermal springs. Sip warm mineral water from a porcelain spa cup, watch the Vřídlo geyser erupt, and stroll from the Mill Colonnade to the Market Colonnade.

Drahovice is a quiet, largely residential hillside neighborhood east of the center. It offers everyday Czech life, leafy streets, cheaper eats, and easy bus links back to the colonnades, making it a calm base away from the spa crowds.

Rybáře is the busy commercial district north of the river, home to shops, supermarkets, the main market area and practical services. It is where locals run errands and where you'll find more affordable dining and lodging.

Tuhnice sits west of the center along the Ohře river and hosts the KV Arena, the Becherovka distillery area and modern apartment blocks. It's a convenient, down-to-earth part of town within a short bus ride of the spa promenade.
Stará Role is a further-out residential suburb to the northwest with a village feel, parks and family homes. It's the most affordable place to stay and connects to the center by frequent city buses.
lodging: Carlsbad Plaza Medical Spa & Wellness Hotel

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink; the hot spring waters are for sipping cures only.

transit.hours: Approx. 4:30-23:00, with night lines on some routes
transit.note: Karlovy Vary has no tram or metro; the DPKV network is entirely city buses. Buy tickets from the driver or machines and validate on board. The compact spa center is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Cash or contactless on board; tickets also via app

air: Karlovy Vary Airport (KLV), 6 km, limited scheduled flights
Most travelers use Prague Airport (PRG), ~122 km
bus: FlixBus, RegioJet and Student Agency coaches connect Prague and Prague Airport (~1h 25m-1h 30m)
Regional and international coaches from Terminal Bus Station
train: Czech Railways (CD) via Karlovy Vary dolni nadrazi and horni nadrazi to Prague, Cheb and Chomutov

transit.m: City bus No. 8 from airport to Trznice (Market) stop (~20-25 min)
Taxi from KLV to spa center (10-15 min)
Most visitors fly into Prague (PRG, ~122 km); FlixBus/RegioJet coach to Karlovy Vary Terminal (~1h 25m-1h 30m, hourly)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants, rounded up or added to the bill
